title: HIV infection
summary: HIV infection (documented per 14.00F1) with one of: A multicentric Castleman disease; B primary CNS lymphoma; C primary effusion lymphoma; D progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy; E pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma; F absolute CD4 ≤50; G absolute CD4 <200 or CD4% <14 with BMI<18.5 (G.1) or hemoglobin<8.0 (G.2); H complication(s) requiring ≥3 hospitalizations within a 12-month period, ≥30 days apart, each lasting ≥48 hours; or I repeated manifestations with constitutional symptoms and one marked functional limitation (I.1, I.2, or I.3).

children.criterion: HIV infection with documentation as described in 14.00F1
One of A through I
Multicentric (not localized or unicentric) Castleman disease affecting multiple groups of lymph nodes or organs containing lymphoid tissue (see 14.00F3a)
Primary central nervous system lymphoma (see 14.00F3b)
Primary effusion lymphoma (see 14.00F3c)
Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (see 14.00F3d)
Pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma (see 14.00F3e)
Absolute CD4 count of 50 cells/mm3 or less (see 14.00F4)
Absolute CD4 count of less than 200 cells/mm3 or CD4 percentage of less than 14 percent, AND one of G.1 (BMI<18.5) or G.2 (hemoglobin<8.0 g/dL) (see 14.00F5)
Absolute CD4 count <200 cells/mm3 OR CD4 percentage <14 percent
G.1 or G.2 (values do not have to be measured on the same date)
BMI measurement of less than 18.5
Hemoglobin measurement of less than 8.0 grams per deciliter (g/dL)

Complication(s) of HIV infection requiring at least three hospitalizations within a 12-month period and at least 30 days apart (see 14.00F6). Each hospitalization must last at least 48 hours, including hours in a hospital emergency department immediately before the hospitalization.

Repeated (as defined in 14.00I3) manifestations of HIV infection (including those listed in 14.11 A-H without the requisite findings, or other manifestations) resulting in significant, documented symptoms or signs (severe fatigue, fever, malaise, involuntary weight loss, headaches, insomnia, nausea, night sweats, pain, or vomiting) AND one of I.1, I.2, or I.3 at the marked level
Repeated manifestations with significant, documented symptoms or signs (severe fatigue, fever, malaise, weight loss, headaches, etc.)
Marked level limitation in one of I.1, I.2, or I.3
Marked limitation of activities of daily living
Marked limitation in maintaining social functioning
Marked limitation in completing tasks in a timely manner due to deficiencies in concentration, persistence, or pace
